title: A Bishop Gift
transcript: The bishop and the knight are very close to this black king. But unfortunately, most of the moves are going to lead to a draw in this position. If for example, I simply move my bishop to this square. Now, this game ends as the board is telling us because this pawn cannot move due to the bishop pinning it to the king and the king cannot go to that square because it's attacked [music] by the knight. And giving this check with the knight doesn't help. The king is simply going to move to the only square available to him. And once it does that, white is technically still winning, but it's going to be harder now that we have allowed these pawns to move. And if white is not careful, it's going to have to sacrifice one of these two pieces for one of the pawns and then draw the game. So why don't we ask the board, what should we play in this position, I have the option to turn on the hints. And once I do that, and we start playing this position, once I touch the pieces, it's going to tell me which one of these moves are good moves. And as you can see, none of these king moves are any good. And as you can see, the knight has no good moves either. But what about the bishop? If I touch this bishop, the board is going to reveal that the winning move is bishop to F6. A brilliant sacrifice. The only move available to black is to capture the bishop. And some of you might think, well, Petro, didn't you tell us that if we lose one of these two pieces, there is going to be no way to checkmate the black king? Well, I did, but this is different [music] because we can force the black king to be stuck in the corner. The only legal move for black is to take another step with this pawn. And now we can finally deliver a checkmate with knight to f7 and win the game. If you like this board, check the first comment.
